goal: Adds a cpu_load field to getpeerinfo showing how much CPU time the message-handling thread has spent on each peer, as a first step toward CPU-based peer monitoring and possible future anti-DoS peer prioritization.
reviewability: Paused: senior reviewers (sipa, ajtowns) raised design-level objections about whether this belongs in production getpeerinfo at all, and the author has not replied since April 2026.
agreement: Disputed. Early concept ACKs from several members (jonatack, sipa, theStack, laanwj, 1440000bytes, BrandonOdiwuor, yuvicc) and a tested ACK (jonatack), plus a weak NACK (rebroad).

Later, sipa argues this metric is exploratory and should be a separate experimental RPC with a decaying average rather than a getpeerinfo field, and ajtowns says the metric is not actionable or comparable across peers (sipa, ajtowns).
Neither concern has been addressed by the author since April 2026.

result.summary: This PR adds a new optional cpu_load field to the getpeerinfo RPC, reporting the CPU time (user + system) the message-handling thread has spent on a given peer, normalized by connection duration. It implements the measurement via clock_gettime on POSIX and GetThreadTimes on Windows, adds a CpuTimer/ThreadCpuTime utility in util/time, and extends bitcoin-cli -netinfo to display the new field. Two commits, with 15 force-pushes reflecting substantial iteration on implementation and wording since January 2025.
result.problem: Node operators and researchers currently have no built-in way to see how much CPU each peer's message processing costs, information that is useful on its own and could eventually support CPU-aware peer prioritization or DoS defenses (referenced issue #31033). The author and several reviewers have empirically observed large (60x+) disparities in per-peer CPU cost, motivating the feature.

open_concerns: sipa (2026-05-26): doubts this belongs in the 'production' getpeerinfo RPC; suggests an explicit experimental resource-usage RPC and a decaying rather than overall average, since many design questions (real time vs CPU time, cross-thread work, weighting useful vs wasted work) remain unresolved.

ajtowns (2026-08-11): argues the metric is not actionable, doesn't distinguish valuable from wasteful peer work, and isn't comparable across peers with different connection durations; suggests raw wall-clock time or per-message-type stats or a flame graph would be more useful.
rebroad (2025-07-28): NACK, calling cpu_load alone a useless metric unless normalized by transactions accepted; author partially agreed this could be a useful addition but not a blocker.
theStack raised a Windows-support documentation gap, which was addressed.
resolved_concerns: ajtowns's question about CPU time vs real time was answered substantively by the author (2026-04-29): CPU time isolates cost attributable to a specific peer, real time is polluted by unrelated system load.
maflcko's concern about single-threaded message handling was acknowledged as valid but deferred to future work if message processing ever becomes multi-threaded.
Several nits from maflcko, fanquake, and jonatack (code style, build-system checks, release-note wording) were implemented across multiple force-pushes.
discussion.author_status: silent since 2026-04-29; sipa's and ajtowns's most recent design objections (May and August 2026) remain unanswered

agreement.reason: Multiple members (jonatack, sipa, theStack, laanwj, 1440000bytes, BrandonOdiwuor, yuvicc) gave concept or tested ACKs early on, and testers (0xB10C, BrandonOdiwuor) confirmed the metric behaves sensibly. However sipa (2026-05-26) argues this should be an experimental separate RPC with a decaying average, and ajtowns (2026-08-11) argues the metric isn't actionable or comparable across peers; both are substantive critiques of the approach, not style nits, and remain open with no author response.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Adds a new field to getpeerinfo's JSON output and updates bitcoin-cli -netinfo; carries the RPC/REST/ZMQ label.
categories.rationale: P3 because it is a new, optional, backwards-compatible field with real but contested value: several reviewers found the numbers meaningful for spotting expensive peers (BrandonOdiwuor's IBD test found a peak cpu_load of 91.7 concentrated in one peer), but sipa and ajtowns argue the field is not actionable or comparable across peers and may belong in a different, experimental interface rather than the stable getpeerinfo RPC. No external consumer has asked for this field specifically; the demand is mostly internal/exploratory (issue #31033).

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: Adds an m_cpu_time field to CNode and CNodeStats, and wraps message processing in CConnman::ThreadMessageHandler with a CpuTimer, changing per-peer stats tracked in net.cpp/net.h.
categories.rationale: P3 because laanwj frames the eventual payoff as anti-DoS measures ('most concretely useful for anti-DoS measures ... reporting it is a still useful first step'), but this PR itself only adds visibility, not a defense, and ajtowns and sipa doubt the specific metric will be the one actually used for that purpose, calling into question how much of that future value this exact implementation captures.

categories.evidence: Adds new ThreadCpuTime()/CpuTimer utilities and an atomic nanoseconds accumulator operator in src/util/time.h/.cpp.
categories.rationale: P4 because this is narrow, single-consumer infrastructure (only used by the CNode CPU-time tracking added in this same PR), not a broadly reused pattern; maflcko flagged a latent correctness assumption (single-threaded message handling) that the author acknowledged but did not need to fix now.

uncertainties: Whether ajtowns's and sipa's most recent objections (August 2026) should be treated as blocking (pushing Agreement to Blocked) or as strong-but-nonblocking design preferences; the text does not use NACK language but the substance is a fundamental design disagreement about the RPC's shape.
Whether the author's absence since April 2026 reflects a considered pause versus simple inactivity; no explicit 'wait' statement was found.
Whether p2p maintainers would consider the m_cpu_time bookkeeping in net.cpp/net.h substantive enough to warrant their own review attention versus treating it as incidental to the RPC feature.
result.card: This PR adds an optional cpu_load field to getpeerinfo, exposing per-peer CPU time spent by the message-handling thread, normalized by connection duration, plus a matching bitcoin-cli -netinfo column and new ThreadCpuTime/CpuTimer utilities. The problem is that operators and researchers currently lack built-in visibility into per-peer CPU cost, which the author and testers (0xB10C, BrandonOdiwuor) confirmed varies by 60x or more and is referenced as a possible first step toward CPU-aware peer prioritization (issue #31033) and future anti-DoS defenses (laanwj). Early concept ACKs came from several members, but the discussion later surfaced unresolved substantive objections: sipa doubts this belongs in the stable getpeerinfo RPC at all and wants an experimental interface with a decaying average, and ajtowns argues the metric isn't actionable or comparable across peers; neither has been addressed since the author's last activity in April 2026. The PR has been through 15 force-pushes over 19 months of iteration and touches rpc, p2p (CNode/ThreadMessageHandler), and utils (new CPU-time helpers), with no external dependency but a stated link to issue #31033.
